title: speckit-backlog — PBI Frontmatter Schema
description: Formal, binding schema for the YAML frontmatter used by every PBI template in this preset. Every Product Backlog Item must validate against exactly one definition selected by its type. The seven PBI types are MAP, EPIC, FEATURE, US, SPIKE, BUG, and TASK. Additional properties are forbidden. Optional keys without values are omitted, never left empty or null. Constraints JSON Schema cannot express are checked by scripts/backlog.py: relations are declared only from the blocked or child PBI, each PBI has at most one PARENT, relation entries follow the canonical order (first by relationType: PARENT, BLOCKED_BY, RELATED; then by type: MAP, EPIC, FEATURE, US, SPIKE, BUG, TASK; then by ascending id), and ids are unique project-wide.

id.description: Project-wide PBI identifier allocated with scripts/backlog.py next-id <TYPE>. It has at least three digits, is unique across the project, matches one of the seven canonical types (MAP, EPIC, FEATURE, US, SPIKE, BUG, TASK), and never changes.

rank.description: Optional priority rank among sibling PBIs sharing the same PARENT (convention: 10, 20, 30...; lower number = higher priority / earlier delivery). Checked against BLOCKED_BY by scripts/backlog.py.

pbiType.description: Type of a PBI. In a PBI's type field it is its own type, fixed by the template used. Inside a relation it is the type of the referenced PBI. Canonical order: MAP, EPIC, FEATURE, US, SPIKE, BUG, TASK.

relationType.description: Nature of the relation. BLOCKED_BY means the referenced PBI blocks the current one. PARENT means the referenced PBI is the current PBI's parent in the hierarchy, at most one. RELATED links PBIs without blocking or hierarchy. Inverse values BLOCKING and CHILD do not exist.

relation.description: A single relation to another PBI.

title.description: Title of the referenced PBI, for readability without resolving its id.

reason.description: Why the relation exists. For BLOCKED_BY, why the current PBI cannot start or close before the referenced one. For PARENT and RELATED, the nature of the link.

relationsMap.description: Map from referenced PBI id to relation. A referenced PBI appears only once. Canonical order: first by relationType (PARENT, BLOCKED_BY, RELATED), then by type (MAP, EPIC, FEATURE, US, SPIKE, BUG, TASK), then by ascending id. scripts/backlog.py checks this writing convention.

url.description: Link to a user-provided attachment such as a mockup, screenshot, recording, log, document, or map photo. Never invent links.

description.description: Short description of what the attachment shows or contains.

mediaMap.description: Map from attachment name to media item.

userStory.description: Frontmatter for pbi-story-template. A User Story is a vertical, independently usable behavior slice.

epic.description: Frontmatter for pbi-epic-template. An Epic frames an open-ended or macro-level goal. It declares a Map as PARENT when it is a Backbone activity; an Epic without a Map has no parent. A Feature under an Epic declares that Epic as its parent.

feature.description: Frontmatter for pbi-feature-template. A Feature is a bounded capability with one Outcome, either a segment of an Epic in a Release Lane or a standalone bounded capability. It declares its Epic as PARENT when it belongs to an Epic.

bug.description: Frontmatter for a Bug PBI. Bugs are not created by this preset's commands; use the spec-kit's bug extension. This schema accepts them for relations and hierarchy.

task.description: Frontmatter for pbi-task-template. Tasks describe technical work for a User Story, a Feature or an Epic, including Walking Skeleton items.

spike.description: Frontmatter for pbi-spike-template. A Spike is timeboxed research that produces knowledge, not production code. The PBI it unblocks declares the Spike with BLOCKED_BY.

map.description: Frontmatter for pbi-map-template. A Map organizes PBIs in its body through the Backbone, Walking Skeleton, and Release Lanes; Backbone Epics declare the Map as PARENT. A Map has a PARENT only in the zoom case, when it breaks down a macro-Epic.
